summary:
Earth Information Jukebox is a web-based application that converts environmental data into sound using data sonification. The project includes three modules: Temperature, Ocean, and Forest, presenting environmental information through interactive graphs and audio. It uses NASA GISTEMP data for global temperature anomalies, NOAA ERSST Version 5 data for ocean temperature, and Our World in Data for global forest area. Python is used to process datasets, while HTML, CSS, and JavaScript are used to develop the web application and generate sound based on numerical values. The project addresses the challenge of relying only on visual methods to understand environmental information by providing an additional audio-based experience. It is important because it makes environmental data exploration more interactive and offers an alternative way for students, researchers, and potentially visually impaired users to experience changes in the Earth's environment.

**Key Features of Earth Information Jukebox**

1. **Three Environmental Modules:** Includes Temperature, Ocean, and Forest modules to explore different environmental datasets.
2. **Data Sonification:** Converts numerical environmental values into sound frequencies, allowing users to hear data variations.
3. **Interactive Graphs:** Displays environmental changes through easy-to-understand visual graphs.
4. **Year-Based Exploration:** Allows users to explore data across different years.
details:
Key Features

  • Three Environmental Modules: Explore Temperature, Ocean, and Forest datasets.
  • Data Sonification: Converts environmental values into sound frequencies.
  • Interactive Data Visualization: Displays environmental changes through graphs.
  • Year-Based Exploration: Explore data across different years.
  • Audio Playback: Play and stop generated data sounds.
  • On-Screen Descriptions: Provides information about selected environmental data.
  • Trusted Data Sources: Uses NASA, NOAA, and Our World in Data datasets.
  • Python Data Processing: Uses Python, Pandas, and NumPy to process datasets.
  • Web-Based Application: Built using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
  • Accessibility Potential: Provides an additional audio-based method for exploring environmental information.
